asphaltened thin liquid films are thicker and much more stable than the films containing maltones and bitumen, and that the stability of asphaltened films is due to their ability to form 3D self-assembled network structure in the film.
asphaltenic thin liquid films exhibit aging, are much more stable than nonasphaltenic thin films, and are stabilized by 3D networks formed by self-assembling of asphaltenic molecules.
the stability and thickness of thin organic liquid emulsion films are controlled by the presence of asphaltenic compounds in heavy oil.

the role of asphaltenic components in the stabilization of thin liquid emulsion film and the effect of the film thickness on the stability of emulsions.

the role of asphaltenic molecules in the formation and stabilization of thin organic liquid emulsion films and provides new insight into the role of asaphaltenes in the stabilization of emulsions and colloidal systems in general.

asphaltenic molecules are able to self-assemble in thin liquid films and form a 3D network, which is responsible for the observed aging and stabilization effects.
the asphaltene nanoaggregates are not responsible for the stabilization of thin liquid emulsion film but rather for the stabilization of the oil/water interface.

the presence of asphaltenic molecules in thin liquid films leads to the formation of a 3D network structure, which is responsible for the stabilization of thin organic liquid emulsion films and the observed slow drainage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
asphaltenic materials are more effective than maltenes in stabilization of thin organic liquid film.
asphaltene-containing thin organic liquid films have unique properties that make them more stable than films formed by maltenes and heavy oil (bitumens).

asphaltenic components of heavy oil and bitumen are able to stabilize thin organic liquid (oil) films and prevent film rupture at very low concentrations, much lower than the maltenic components of heavy oils and bitumen.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the asphaltenes play a key role in stabilizing thin organic liquid films and in controlling the drainage kinetics and the film stability.
the presence of asphaltenic compounds in the organic phase of thin liquid film significantly changes the film properties and stability compared to the films stabilized by maltenese or bitumen.
asphaltenic materials are capable of self-organization in thin films to form a 3D network that stabilizes thin organic liquid films against rupture and drainage.
